clue.text: A quality the city speculator may be anxious to develop

definitions.meaning: a quality or attribute, as in the properties of a metal

definitions.text: the city speculator may be anxious to develop
definitions.meaning: land and buildings that a developer in the City buys to build on

explanation.surface: A trait that a City speculator is keen to cultivate.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a personal quality the speculator wants to grow; the second sense is real estate, which property developers build on.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic is called a property, and real estate held as an asset is also property.

clue.text: Man of God who should be able to handle a crook

definitions.text: Man of God who should be able to handle a crook

parts.words: Man of God who should be able to handle a crook
parts.note: a clergyman is a shepherd of his flock and carries a shepherd's crook, not a criminal

explanation.surface: A clergyman ought to be able to cope with a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' suggests a criminal the priest must reform; it is the shepherd's staff, and the word for this clergyman is Latin for shepherd.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister in charge of a congregation is named from the Latin for shepherd, whose staff is a crook.

clue.text: Some of the phlox Alistair mistook for wood-sorrel

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Alistair confused some of his phlox with a woodland plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood-sorrel is a common plant of the genus whose name is the botanical term here; the clue's 'mistook for' is a link.

clue.text: I grew restive about a garden pest

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
restive means restless and fidgety, so the letters of the two words will not stay put

explanation.surface: A gardener grows impatient with an insect damaging the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restive' rearranges I GREW to ERWIG, and 'about' puts that round A: E(A)RWIG.
explanation.definitionFit: This small insect with pincers chews flowers and is a familiar pest in gardens.

clue.text: The breakdown firm's line of business?

definitions.text: The breakdown firm's line of business?

parts.words: The breakdown firm's line of business?
parts.note: a recovery company's 'line' is literally the rope or cable it uses to pull cars, not its trade

explanation.surface: What does a vehicle recovery company do for a living?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line of business' normally means trade; here the line is a physical cord used to haul broken-down cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown truck hauls disabled cars with a cable, the literal 'line' of its work.

clue.text: Thwarted by ill-will, it raced around

indicators.note: around says the word for raced goes round the other piece

parts.note: raced means went fast, sped

explanation.surface: Someone frustrated out of malice dashes about.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'Thwarted by ill-will', not just 'Thwarted'; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To spite someone is to frustrate them out of malice.

clue.text: Set forth the case for sterling

parts.note: the arguments in favour are the pros
the pound is the British currency, sterling

explanation.surface: A lawyer presents the argument in favour of the British currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound is to put forward an idea for consideration.

clue.text: It naturally takes them some time to go from green to red

definitions.text: It naturally takes them some time to go from green to red

parts.words: It naturally takes them some time to go from green to red
parts.note: these salad fruits ripen from green to red on the vine, not traffic lights changing

explanation.surface: A slow traffic light seems to take ages to change colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Green to red suggests traffic lights, but 'naturally' points to ripening fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: These red salad fruits start green and ripen slowly on the plant.

clue.text: Official visit to remind the soldier he's wanted?

definitions.meaning: a visit paid out of obligation rather than pleasure

definitions.text: to remind the soldier he's wanted?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a summons calling a soldier back to his obligations

explanation.surface: A formal call reminds a soldier he is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit made from obligation is named this, and literally it is the summons of obligation.

clue.text: Box files for chirpy air travellers?

parts.note: to box is to spar
files are lines or rows

explanation.surface: Office storage boxes for cheerful airline passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box files' reads as office stationery; it is two pieces, a verb and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: These small chirping birds travel by air.

clue.text: The shape of the book put at the end of the bench

indicators.note: put, with 'the end of', places the word at after the bench word

parts.note: a form is a long backless bench, as in a schoolroom

explanation.surface: A book's layout is set at the end of the workbench.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a long backless bench of the kind once used in British schoolrooms; 'put' with 'the end of' places the little word last.
explanation.definitionFit: Format is the size and layout of a printed book.

clue.text: Vegetables holding sanctimonious views

indicators.note: holding says the vegetables enclose the other piece

parts.note: onions are vegetables
pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: Vegetable growers with self-righteous attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi, short for pious, is a standard crossword word for sanctimonious; 'holding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions are views held by people.

clue.text: Caught the eye of the Christian community in Egypt

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
optic is an old or humorous word for the eye

explanation.surface: Something caught the attention of Egypt's Christians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught the eye' reads as an idiom for attracting notice; it is C plus a word for the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coptic Church is the ancient Christian church of Egypt.

clue.text: Girl guides at film show

parts.note: not the youth organisation but women who lead patrons to their seats in a cinema

explanation.surface: Members of the Girl Guides attend a cinema screening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl guides' looks like the scouting movement; here they are women showing people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Women employed in a cinema to lead patrons to their seats.

clue.text: If I get time I'll have to go there!

definitions.text: If I get time I'll have to go there!

parts.words: If I get time I'll have to go there!
parts.note: 'get time' means receive a jail sentence, not find a spare moment

explanation.surface: A busy person promises to visit somewhere when free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get time' sounds like finding leisure; in criminal slang 'time' is a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict sentenced to time is locked in this small room in jail.

clue.text: The main way to get from the Soviet Union to Turkey

definitions.text: The main way to get from the Soviet Union to Turkey

parts.words: The main way to get from the Soviet Union to Turkey
parts.note: 'the main' is the sea, so the route is by water across the inland sea between them

explanation.surface: The principal route from the USSR to Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea, so 'main way' is a sea route, not the chief route.
explanation.definitionFit: This inland sea lies between the former Soviet coast and northern Turkey.

clue.text: Upset voter redirected to the ballot-box?

indicators.note: redirected means sent another way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: an urn is a ballot box

explanation.surface: An angry voter is sent to the polling station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like a description of the voter, but it is the definition; 'redirected' signals the anagram, and the ballot-box follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn is to upset or tip over.

clue.text: A kind of grey coat

indicators.note: of here means made of, so the answer is formed from these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A grey overcoat of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator is slight: the answer is made 'of' the letters of GREY COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a class or sort of thing.

clue.text: Eros given pippins for 7, maybe

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
pippins are varieties of apples

explanation.surface: Cupid is presented with apples in place of salad fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to the answer at 7-down, an old name for which is this.
explanation.definitionFit: Love apple is an old name for the tomato, the 7-down answer.

clue.text: Hired out duck shed built against a wall

annotationWithheld.why: Hired out duck shed built against a wall: LENT (hired out) + O (duck) gives LENTO; the A of LEAN-TO has no clue word, so a word such as 'a' seems lost and no scan is held
annotationWithheld.clue: Hired out duck shed built against a wall

clue.text: A ship laden with fruit or arms for warring tribes, perhaps

indicators.note: laden with means carrying a cargo, so the ship holds the fruit

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A cargo vessel carries fruit or weapons for tribes at war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A ship' reads as one vessel, but the clue wants the steamship abbreviation; 'laden with' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spears are thrusting weapons used in tribal warfare.

clue.text: Stop at the foot of a South Carolina mount

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the foot of places the stop word below the earlier pieces

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for the US state of South Carolina
to stop is to end

explanation.surface: Halt at the base of a mountain in South Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a noun for a hill; it is the verb, to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount is to climb or go up.

clue.text: The angle from which a goal may be headed in?

definitions.text: The angle from which a goal may be headed in?

parts.words: The angle from which a goal may be headed in?
parts.note: in football, a kick from the angle of the pitch is often headed into the net

explanation.surface: From what angle might a footballer head the ball into the net?
explanation.walkthrough: A football corner kick is taken from the angle of the pitch and is often met with a header.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle where two lines meet, and in football a kick taken from that point of the pitch.

clue.text: Old recipes people pay to get

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for cooking instructions
a shop gives proof of payment after a purchase

explanation.surface: Antique cookbooks that people pay money for.
explanation.definitionFit: The word once meant cooking formulas, and today means written proof of payment or takings.

clue.text: Lethargic result of misreading Proust

indicators.note: misreading means reading wrongly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting Proust wrong leaves a reader drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Proust's long novel has a reputation for sending readers to sleep, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed, sluggish state.

clue.text: An individual in step before history began

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for step

parts.note: a step in a process is a stage
an individual is one

explanation.surface: Someone keeping pace in prehistoric times.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a period, the prehistoric era, rather than a time adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest prehistoric period, when tools were made of flint.

clue.text: Troubles any son gets involved in

indicators.note: gets involved in suggests mixing these letters together into a new order

explanation.surface: Any son's problems spread to the family.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy is to bother or irritate, and troubles here is a verb.

clue.text: Took up the cause and entered a union?

definitions.meaning: married, the old sense of the verb

explanation.surface: A campaigner backed the cause and then got married.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse means both to adopt a belief and to marry.
